title: Screw-clamp ground (PE) terminal block, 4 mm² class, green-yellow

sources.citation: game-design: unverified product class. Screw-clamp feed-through DIN-rail terminal blocks of the 4 mm² class are about 6.2 mm wide per pole (2.5 mm² blocks about 5.2 mm), roughly 45 to 50 mm tall and deep, as makers’ datasheets list them (recalled, not read in this PR). Drawn 6 × 48 × 42 mm: the width is rounded down to whole mm (so 10 blocks take 60 mm, not 62). Green-yellow, the colour of protective-earth blocks; a real PE block bonds its foot to the rail (P4 grounding, not modelled in P3). Two clamps, one at the top (1) and one at the bottom (2); conductors enter the top and bottom faces.

game-design: clips onto a 35 mm top-hat rail (IEC 60715, cited by number), 6 mm along it, centred on the rail: its origin sits 45 − 24 = 21 mm above the mount origin (DIN 43880’s 90 mm modular-device line, ADR 0015 note 7), so its 48 mm body spans the rail centreline ± 24 mm.

game-design: unverified. The 4 mm² class is marked for copper only, 22 to 10 AWG solid or stranded (bare or in a ferrule), with a rising-cage (box) clamp tightened by an M3 screw to about 0.5 to 0.8 N·m; the fictional block is marked 0.6 N·m (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D), cited by number, requires the marked value) with a 9 ± 1 mm strip and an 8 mm cage. One conductor is rated; a second fits under the cage and makes a worse termination (D8). No UL 486A-B torque table is used.

game-design: unverified. Terminal-block clamp screws commonly take a slotted blade, many with a Pozidriv combination head (common practice, not read from one datasheet); the drive type is a name and its size is not modelled.

game-design: the screw clamps take the branch-circuit screw class’s contact resistance, 0.3 mΩ at the marked torque with copper at 20 °C (NBS Building Science Series 103, 1977, measured 0.2 to 0.5 mΩ on good branch-circuit screw terminals; ADR 0018 §4.1), and its calibrated 0.026 W/K heat path (§3.3). BSS 103 measured wiring-device terminals, not terminal-block cages, so applying it is a game-design choice. The cage’s heat capacity, 0.5 J/K, is the DIN supply’s small-box-clamp estimate (about 1.3 g of brass and steel × about 380 J/(kg·K)).
